description: Syrian Air Force MiG-21R displayed outdoors on the Syrian side of the October War Panorama, fitted with two AA-2 Atoll missiles and two UB-16 rocket pods. The Aviationist noted in 2008 that it had been repainted in a scheme and roundels quite different from the original. Esri imagery of 31 May 2025 shows a delta-wing aircraft and a helicopter still standing on the northern hardstand alongside rows of armoured vehicles, so the outdoor display survived the war and the change of government.

Syrian Air Force Mil Mi-8 displayed outdoors at the October War Panorama carrying four UB-16 rocket pods. The Aviationist recorded it in 2008 as coded 78 and repainted; spottingmode carries it as 1278. Confirmed still present as a rotor-bearing airframe on Esri imagery of 31 May 2025.

Remains of an Israeli Air Force F-4 Phantom shot down over Lebanon, displayed as a war trophy on the Israeli side of the panorama's cylindrical main building. No serial or identifying marks are visible on it and none is published, so the tail number is blank. Wreckage deliberately retained and publicly exhibited in a museum is treated here as an exhibit rather than as battlefield debris. OpenStreetMap maps a third aircraft at this site tagged as destroyed and ruined which is consistent with this airframe.
